title: The two-sided coin — 12 machine-checked theorems of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit and how they are bound
description:
The two-sided coin — 12 machine-checked theorems of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit, one Lean namespace, wing the ring. 12 close by exhaustion over a finite domain (by decide). Every one is sealed live in the append-only ledger.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used in this deposit's honest sense: correlation by derivation, not quantum entanglement, and no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 7 definition(s) are used by two or more theorems, binding 79 pair(s); the theorems fall into 1 strand(s), the largest of 12. Most binding: refl (9), digits (8), tetB (3), tetA (3), axis (3), fall (3).

2 · Imports. Built on: no other cluster. Built on it: no other cluster. Checking this cluster needs 1 file(s): src/proof/coin.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 12 sealed receipts fold to e085bd35-36da-8011-a2b1-f08c6394f507. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed on this run. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (6, 5, 7, 7, 8, 6, 6). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs observed among each theorem's seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: reach.lean (3 observed, 0.67 expected, lift 4.51), generated.lean (4 observed, 1.73 expected, lift 2.31), light.lean (4 observed, 1.73 expected, lift 2.31). A lift near 1 is what chance gives. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 15.39; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.53. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). Chance, measured: over 200 reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to (seeded, so every rebuild gives the same numbers), a best lift at least this high arose in 6.5% of them — consistent with chance.

Prior art. the reflection d ↦ 10 − d is the TEN'S COMPLEMENT, and its sibling 9 − d the nines' complement — the method of complements, used to turn subtraction into addition in Pascal's calculator (1642), the Comptometer and the Curta, and in modern computer arithmetic. That it is an involution with a single fixed point is the property those machines rely on. Searched 2026-09-04, term "method of complements / nines' complement / ten's complement"; prior art found and credited Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json. No novelty is claimed here.

The theorems.

  1. the_reflection_is_an_involution — digits.all (fun d => refl (refl d) == d) record
  2. one_side_is_reflected_onto_itself — tetB.all (fun d => tetB.contains (refl d)) record
  3. the_other_two_swap — tetA.all (fun d => axis.contains (refl d)) ∧ axis.all (fun d => tetA.contains (refl d)) record
  4. exactly_one_digit_is_unmoved — (digits.filter (fun d => refl d == d)) = [5] record
  5. exactly_one_digit_reflects_out_of_range — (digits.filter (fun d => refl d > 9)) = [0] ∧ refl 0 = 10 record
  6. the_classes_partition_the_nine — tetA.length + tetB.length + axis.length = 9 ∧ (tetA ++ tetB ++ axis).eraseDups.length = 9 ∧ digits.length = 10 record
  7. every_digit_is_sorted_exactly_once — digits.all (fun d => (tetB.contains d && tetB.contains (refl d)) || (tetA.contains d && axis.contains (refl d)) || (axis.contains d && tetA.contains (refl d)) || (refl d == d) || (refl d > 9)) record
  8. the_fall_fixes_every_digit_but_the_void — (digits.filter (fun d => fall d != d)) = [0] ∧ nonzero.all (fun d => fall d == d) record
  9. the_fall_and_the_reflection_share_one_exceptional_digit — (digits.filter (fun d => fall d != d)) = (digits.filter (fun d => refl d > 9)) record
  10. on_the_fixed_points_the_reflection_never_leaves — nonzero.all (fun d => refl d >= 1 && refl d <= 9) ∧ nonzero.all (fun d => refl (refl d) == d) record
  11. what_escapes_falls_back_inside — refl 0 = 10 ∧ fall 10 = 1 ∧ nonzero.contains (fall 10) record
  12. the_nines_complement_pairs_the_ten_digits — digits.all (fun d => digits.contains (9 - d) && 9 - (9 - d) == d && 9 - d != d) ∧ (digits.filter (fun d => d < 9 - d)).length * 2 = digits.length record
